scripts.dialogHint: Saved to the team's library and available on every server you run it on.
scripts.deleteBody: Its run history is kept, but the script itself can no longer be run.
scripts.emptyHint: Add a script to the team's library, or run one of the built-ins below.

builtins.title: Built-in installs
builtins.hint: Read-only, one-click installs for common host software on Debian and Ubuntu servers (Caddy, PHP, Composer, Node.js, MySQL/MariaDB, Redis, phpMyAdmin, Chromium).

runs.title: Run history
runs.hint: Every run of a script or a built-in install, across every server it targeted.
runs.viewHint: One tab per target server, streamed live while it runs.

runDialog.title: Run {name}
runDialog.hint: Choose one or more servers. Output streams live once it starts.
runDialog.noServers: No enrolled servers on this team yet.

mail.hint: Run your own mail server, on your own server. Install Stalwart, add domains, mailboxes and aliases, and check or publish the DNS records each domain needs. Installing, adding and removing needs owner or admin; any member can view.

servers.title: Mail servers
servers.hint: A Stalwart mail server installed on one of the team's own enrolled servers.
servers.installHint: Installs Stalwart on the chosen server and opens its admin API on an internal port. The hostname is the server's own HELO/PTR name, e.g. mail.example.com.
servers.hostnameHint: Must match this server's reverse DNS (PTR) for outgoing mail to be trusted.
servers.noServers: No enrolled servers on this team yet.
servers.emptyHint: Install Stalwart on one of the team's enrolled servers to start hosting mail.
servers.deleteBody: Removes the mail server and every domain, mailbox and alias hosted on it. This cannot be undone.

domains.title: Domains
domains.hint: Domains hosted on the team's mail servers, each with its own mailboxes and aliases.
domains.addHint: Adds a domain to the chosen mail server. DNS records still need to be checked and published for mail to flow.
domains.needServer: Install a mail server first, then add a domain to it.
domains.deleteBody: Removes the domain and every mailbox and alias on it. This cannot be undone.

mailboxes.title: Mailboxes
mailboxes.addHint: Hosbah generates a password and shows it once. It is never stored in the clear.
mailboxes.quotaHint: Storage limit for this mailbox, in megabytes.
mailboxes.passwordHint: Shown once. Copy it now — Hosbah does not keep it.
mailboxes.deleteBody: The mailbox and its mail are removed from the server. This cannot be undone.

aliases.title: Aliases and forwards
aliases.addHint: An alias fans out to one or more mailboxes on this domain. A forward sends to external addresses.
aliases.destHintAlias: One or more mailbox addresses on this domain, separated by commas.
aliases.destHintForward: One or more external email addresses, separated by commas.

siteTemplates.title: Templates
siteTemplates.hint: Declarative YAML that scaffolds a ready-to-deploy app in one step: driver, build, env defaults and any data services it needs. Built-in templates plus whatever the team has saved.
siteTemplates.emptyHint: Save a YAML template, or preview and use one of Hosbah's built-ins.
siteTemplates.yamlHint: Unknown keys are rejected. Env values may reference generated secrets ({{random:32}}) or a provisioned service's URL ({{db.url}}).
siteTemplates.dialogHint: Saved to the team's library. Built-in template names can't be reused.
siteTemplates.deleteBody: Apps already created from this template are not affected.
siteTemplates.previewHint: What this template will create. Secret values stay hidden until an app is actually created.
siteTemplates.createFromHint: Creates the app on the chosen server and sets its environment from this template.
siteTemplates.noServers: No enrolled servers on this team yet.

products.title: Products
products.hint: Turn an app, a catalogue recipe or a repo into a SaaS product: per-customer instances, each with its own hostname, env and lifecycle. Managing products and instances needs owner, admin or deployer; archiving, destroying and API keys need owner or admin.
products.name: Name
products.sourceKindHint: How this product's instances are built. All three deploy the same way — this is only for display.
products.dialogHint: Every instance is a normal app under the hood, so its logs, deployments and domain keep working the usual way.
products.nameHint: Lowercase letters, digits and dashes; unique in the team.
products.archiveBody: No new instances may be provisioned, but existing instances are untouched.
products.emptyHint: Turn an app you already run, a catalogue recipe, or a repository into a SaaS product.

instances.dialogHint: Its own app, its own env, its own hostname — nothing is shared with other instances.
instances.customerHint: The team's own identifier for this customer (shown back on webhooks).
instances.name: Instance name
instances.namePlaceholder: Derived from the customer reference if left blank
instances.noServers: No enrolled servers on this team yet.
instances.envHint: One KEY=value per line. Extends the product's own defaults for this instance only.
instances.destroyConfirm: Type {name} to confirm. Its app, containers and images go too — this cannot be undone.

keys.dialogHint: A product-scoped API key for the team's own billing or signup system. It can only touch this product's instances.
keys.name: Name
keys.webhookHint: Optional. Receives a signed POST on every instance state change.
keys.revokeBody: Any request signed with this key stops working at once.
keys.mintedHint: Shown once. Store it in your billing system now — it cannot be shown again.

api.hint: Examples for {name}'s public, key-authenticated instance API — for your own billing or signup system, never a browser session.
api.webhookHint: Every call is signed: X-Hosbah-Signature: sha256=<hex HMAC-SHA256 of the raw body with the webhook secret>.

sites.title: Sites
sites.hint: Apps running on this server, and its proxy hosts. Open a site to see its canvas.
sites.empty: No sites on this server yet.
sites.workersHint: Workers come from [processes] in hosbah.toml and deploy with the app.
sites.addDatabaseHint: PostgreSQL or MySQL on this server
sites.addBucketHint: S3-compatible object storage (MinIO) on this server
sites.addServiceHint: Provisioned on {server}. Attach it to the app from its page once it is running.

tunnels.title: Tunnels
tunnels.hint: How this server is reached when it has no public address.

sftp.title: SFTP users
sftp.hint: Chrooted, sftp-only system accounts (no shell) so a team can upload and download files with any SFTP client — FileZilla, WinSCP — without sharing root.
sftp.addHint: Paste a public key, have Hosbah generate a password, or both. The user is chrooted to its root directory and can't see outside it.
sftp.emptyHint: Add one to hand out upload/download access without sharing root.
sftp.usernameHint: Lowercase, starts with a letter or underscore, up to 32 characters.
sftp.rootDirHint: Absolute path on the server. The user is chrooted to it and can't see outside it.
sftp.publicKeysHint: One OpenSSH public key per line (ssh-ed25519, ssh-rsa, …). Replaces the existing keys when changed.
sftp.passwordShown: Password (shown once) — copy it now, Hosbah won't show it again.
sftp.editHint: The username cannot change; remove the user and add another for that.
sftp.removeConfirm: Remove sftp user {user} from {server}? Its access ends at once.

imported.noticeApp: Hosbah found this site already running on the server and manages it through the server's agent: power, domains with HTTPS, resources, snapshots and backups. Deploying from git applies only to apps Hosbah builds.
imported.noticeDatabase: Hosbah found this database already running on the server. Control its power here; add its admin login to manage its databases, users and backups like any Hosbah database.
imported.removeHint: Hosbah stops showing it. The workload keeps running on the server, untouched.
imported.removeConfirmBody: Only the record is removed; {name} keeps running on the server. Hosbah will not import it again.

controls.queued: Sent to the server. Its progress shows below.
controls.powerHint: Runs on the server through its Hosbah agent. Every action is audited.
controls.restartBody: It stops and starts again; visitors see a short interruption.
controls.shutdownBody: Asks the guest's operating system to power off cleanly. It stays off until started.
controls.stopBody: The container stops and stays stopped until started.
controls.forceStopBody: Cuts the guest's power immediately, like pulling the plug — unsaved work inside it is lost.
controls.statsHint: CPU, memory and disk right now, read from the server.
controls.statsNone: The server did not answer in time. Try again in a moment.
controls.logsHint: The container's recent output. Follow keeps streaming new lines for a while.
controls.domainsHint: Point a hostname at it: Hosbah routes it with HTTPS and, with Cloudflare, creates the DNS.
controls.domainPortGuest: The port the site listens on inside the guest (e.g. 80 or 3000).
controls.domainPortContainer: The published port on the server. Empty: its first published port.
controls.resizeHint: vCPUs and memory apply at once for LXC (VMs may need a restart). Disks only grow.
controls.diskGrowHint: Adds space to the root disk. It cannot be shrunk afterwards.
controls.snapshotsHint: A point in time you can roll back to — take one before an upgrade.
controls.rollbackBody: {name} returns to exactly how it was at {snap}; everything since is lost.
controls.deleteSnapshotBody: You can no longer roll back to {snap}. The site itself is not affected.
controls.backupHint: A full copy of the guest on the server's backup storage, restorable from Proxmox.
controls.recreateHint: Pulls its image again and recreates it with the same settings, ports and volumes.
controls.recreateBody: The container is replaced by a new one from the latest image with the same settings. The old one is kept until the new one runs.
controls.destroyGuestHint: Stops and deletes the guest from Proxmox, then its record here. Cannot be undone.
controls.destroyContainerHint: Removes the container from the server, then its record here. Cannot be undone.
controls.purgeGuest: Also delete its disks and backups (purge)
controls.credentialsHint: Add the database's admin user so Hosbah can manage its databases, users and backups.
controls.dbNameHint: Optional: the database to connect to.
controls.credentialsVerified: Connected ({version}). Its databases, users and backups are now managed here.

home.serversHint: Every server of this team — its health right now, the last hour, and what shipped to it last.
home.noReport: No report from its agent yet.
home.noDeploys: No deploys on this server yet.
home.search: Search by name, IP or system

github.title: GitHub
github.hint: Sign this server in to GitHub (the GitHub CLI on the server) to pick repositories for new apps and deploy private ones.
github.tokenHint: A GitHub token with repo access. It is sealed to this server's agent and never shown again.
github.starting: Installing the GitHub CLI and starting the sign-in on the server…
github.deviceIntro: Enter this one-time code on GitHub to let this server use your account:
github.deviceWaiting: Waiting for you to approve it on GitHub — this page updates by itself. The code expires in 15 minutes.
github.connected: GitHub is connected on this server.
github.failed: The sign-in did not finish. Try again.
github.disconnectBody: The server signs out of GitHub; private repositories can no longer be deployed on it until you connect again.
github.askAdmin: An owner or admin can connect GitHub on this server.
github.pickRepoHint: From the GitHub account connected on the chosen server.
github.connectFirst: Connect GitHub on this server to pick from your repositories.

app.title: GitHub App
app.hint: Install Hosbah’s GitHub App on a GitHub account or organisation: its repositories appear in New site, deploys clone them with a short-lived token, and pushes deploy automatically.
app.notConfigured: The GitHub App is not set up on this platform.
app.none: Not installed on any GitHub account yet.
app.askAdmin: An owner or admin can install the GitHub App.
app.requested: GitHub asked an organisation owner to approve the installation. It appears here once they do.

errors.state_invalid: That installation link expired or was opened in another browser. Start again.
errors.installation_unknown: GitHub does not know that installation. Start again.
errors.installation_taken: That GitHub account’s installation is already connected to another team.
errors.github_unavailable: GitHub could not be reached to confirm the installation. Try again.
errors.not_configured: The GitHub App is not set up on this platform.
errors.forbidden: Only an owner or admin of the team can install the GitHub App.
errors.internal: Something went wrong on our side. Try again.

app.fromAppHint: Repositories the team’s GitHub App installations can reach. Deploys clone them with a short-lived installation token.

lists.searchApps: Search apps by name, branch, domain…
lists.searchDatabases: Search databases by name, kind, endpoint…
lists.searchSftp: Search by username or root directory…
lists.deleteAppBody: Its containers, releases and domains are removed from the server. This cannot be undone.
lists.deleteDatabaseBody: Its container and volume are removed from the server, data included. This cannot be undone.
lists.editAppHint: Changes apply from the next deploy.
lists.editProxyHint: The hostname cannot change; remove the host and add another for that.
lists.noTunnels: No tunnel is open on this server.
lists.noTunnelCreds: Add an frp or Tailscale credential first, then open a tunnel here.

site.title: Title
site.titleHint: Shown instead of {name}. The name in URLs and on the server does not change.
site.appearanceHint: How this site looks in lists, on the home page and in its header.
site.deploymentsHint: Every deploy with its live log. Roll back to the previous release or restart the running one.
site.environmentHint: Sealed variables, applied on the next deploy or restart.
site.databasesHint: Data services on this site's server. Attaching injects a sealed DATABASE_URL or REDIS_URL.
site.databasesEmpty: Create a Postgres, MySQL or Redis service on this server, then attach it here.
site.attached: Attached as {variable}; it applies on the next deploy or restart.
site.injected: Connection variables set on this site:
site.connectedServicesHint: What this site's environment was detected pointing at: shared infrastructure and data services alike.
site.connectedServicesEmpty: No connection variables matched a known service yet.
site.workersHint: The processes this site runs besides web, as its hosbah.toml declares them.
site.workersEmptyHint: Add a [processes] entry to hosbah.toml (a queue worker, a scheduler, a Go routine runner) and deploy.
site.workersNote: Workers start after the health gate on every deploy and drain with the old release. Per-worker scaling and restarts are coming.
site.logsGuest: Logs are read from containers. For a guest, open its console on the server.
site.proxyHint: Hostnames Caddy serves for this site, with HTTPS. Each one needs a DNS record pointing at the server.
site.backupsHint: Snapshots and backups of what this site runs on.
site.backupsDataHint: A git-deployed site is rebuilt from its repository; what needs backing up is its databases. Schedules and restores are on each database.

php.title: PHP
php.hint: The PHP version to build with and php.ini overrides, applied on the next deploy.
php.versionHint: Pins the PHP version Railpack builds with. Auto lets Railpack detect it from composer.json.
php.iniHint: Applied as a php.ini on top of the image's defaults. Only a fixed set of safe keys is allowed.
php.invalidValue: That value isn't allowed: no ";", "[", "]" or line breaks.

deployScript.hint: How this site builds and releases on every deploy: the mode, the preset it started from, and each pipeline step.

modeHints.auto: Hosbah picks full only when the Dockerfile, lockfiles or base image change.
modeHints.fast: Build the binary on the server, no Docker rebuild.

deployScript.presetHint: Fills the steps below with that stack's default pipeline. Choosing a different preset overwrites your edited steps.
deployScript.presetConfirmBody: Switching presets replaces every step below with that preset's defaults. Your unsaved edits will be lost.
deployScript.stepsEmpty: No steps yet. Add one below.
deployScript.historyHint: Every saved version of {name}'s deploy script, newest first.
deployScript.restoreConfirmBody: Restoring version {version} makes it the current deploy script, and adds a new version to the history.
deployScript.advancedHint: For an app with no Dockerfile: run the pipeline steps in a separate builder image, then copy the outputs onto the current runtime image. Leave the builder image empty to run the steps in place instead.
deployScript.outputsHint: Paths, relative to the checkout, copied onto the runtime image once the builder image's steps ran.

flow.title: How a request reaches this site
flow.hint: Click any stop to manage it.

canvas.hint: Drag boxes to arrange them, click one to manage it, add a component with +, or drag from the site's handle to a database to connect it.
canvas.hintReadOnly: Click any box to manage it. You can arrange the view; your role cannot save it or change the site.
canvas.label: Site canvas
canvas.saveFailed: The layout could not be saved.
canvas.addHint: Pick what to add; it appears on the canvas already connected to the site.
canvas.attachHint: The site gets a sealed connection variable from its next deploy or restart. You can also drag from the site's handle to a database box.
canvas.noAttachable: Every running database on this server is already connected, or there is none yet.

add.domain: Route a hostname to this site through Caddy
add.database: Connect a database or cache running on this server
add.bucket: An S3 bucket on this server's MinIO, with its own key
add.needsMinio: Needs a MinIO service on this server first
add.browser: Headless Chromium the site can drive
add.monitor: An uptime check or a CPU, memory or disk alert
add.schedule: A cron job run inside the live release
add.realtime: Send websocket traffic to one of the site's workers
add.stack: Start a new site from this stack

a11y.node: Press Enter to open its section, Delete to remove it, or the arrow keys to move it.
a11y.nodeReadOnly: Press Enter to open its section, or the arrow keys to move it.
a11y.edge: Press Delete to remove this connection.

repository.hint: The repository behind this site, read through gh on its server.
repository.p1: Recent commits on the deployed branch, with which one is live
repository.p2: Changes between the live release and the branch head
repository.p3: Deploy any commit, or switch branch
repository.p4: Open pull requests and their checks

storage.hint: Files this site keeps outside its releases.
storage.p1: Persistent volumes mounted into every release
storage.p2: S3-compatible buckets (MinIO) with sealed credentials injected

queues.p1: Laravel queues / Horizon, BullMQ, Asynq and Celery detected from the app
queues.p2: Pending, running and failed jobs per queue
queues.p4: Alerts when a queue backs up

schedules.hint: Cron jobs run inside the site's release.
schedules.p1: Schedules with a cron expression and a command
schedules.p2: Each run's output and exit code, kept
schedules.p4: An alert when a run fails or is late

realtime.p1: Laravel Reverb, Socket.IO / ws for Node, and Go websocket servers
realtime.p2: Runs as its own process with Caddy routing websockets to it

browsers.hint: Headless browsers this site can drive, like Chromebox.
browsers.p1: Create a browser on the server with a CDP endpoint injected as an env var
browsers.p2: For crawling, screenshots, PDFs and tests
browsers.p4: Limits on memory, sessions and idle time

stacks.hint: Ready apps and starter stacks, installed in one step.
stacks.p1: Apps to connect: SearXNG, Firecrawl, Evolution API, OpenSEO, mail services
stacks.p2: Starter stacks for a new site: Laravel, Laravilt, Laravel with TomatoPHP, togo
stacks.p3: A catalog anyone can publish to: a recipe is a manifest plus scripts
stacks.p4: Each install wires its env vars, domain and database

monitors.hint: Know when something is wrong before visitors do.
monitors.p1: Uptime checks on each hostname, from outside
monitors.p2: Rules on CPU, memory, disk and response time
monitors.p3: Notify by email, webhook, Telegram or WhatsApp
monitors.p4: Incident history with what fired and when it recovered

dns.hint: Cloudflare DNS records and certificates for this site's hostnames.
dns.p1: Records for each hostname, created and repaired from here
dns.p3: Certificate issuer, expiry and renewals from Caddy
dns.p4: Force HTTPS, HSTS and redirects between hostnames

repo.behind: live is {n} behind the branch history
repo.commitsHint: On the deployed branch, newest first. Deploy any of them.
repo.noCommits: No commits found on this branch.
repo.search: Search by message, author or sha…
repo.fullRebuildHint: Skips the fast track and rebuilds the image from scratch.
repo.truncated: The list is cut short; open the compare on GitHub for the rest.

dns.recordsHint: Each hostname should point at this site's server ({address}).
dns.recordsHintPrivate: This server has only a private address, so no public record applies.
dns.none: This site has no hostnames yet. Add one in the proxy manager.
dns.noZone: No Cloudflare credential of this team holds this zone
dns.takeoverBody: Hosbah did not create this record. It is {old} and will become {next}.
dns.deleteBody: The hostname stops resolving until a record exists again.
dns.certsHint: What Caddy serves for each hostname; public certificates renew on their own.
dns.certsOffline: The server is offline or did not answer, so certificates could not be read.

analytics.hint: Traffic through this site's hostnames, read from the Caddy proxy.
analytics.emptyHint: Analytics appear once requests reach this site through its hostnames.

rum.title: Real-user monitoring
rum.hint: Core Web Vitals reported by this app's own visitors' browsers — no synthetic checks, just what people actually experienced.
rum.enableHint: Adds a tiny beacon script to the snippet below; paste it into the app's pages to start collecting.
rum.once: Copy it now. The key is shown only once; Hosbah keeps only its hash.
rum.rotateHint: The current key stops working immediately; visitors using it are silently dropped, never shown an error.
rum.snippetHidden: A key already exists; its snippet was shown once when it was created. Rotate to get a new one.
rum.snippetHiddenHint: Rotate to get a new one.
rum.vitalsHint: p75 per metric, rated good / needs improvement / poor against Google's published thresholds.
rum.emptyHint: Core Web Vitals appear once the beacon snippet is live on the app's pages and visitors load it.

apm.title: APM: traces and exceptions
apm.hint: Slow endpoints and grouped exceptions, built from what the app's own OpenTelemetry SDK exports — no code beyond the standard SDK.
apm.enableHint: Mints a secret ingest key and shows the env snippet once; it is also auto-injected into the app's own env on its next deploy.
apm.once: Copy it now. The key is a real secret, shown only once; Hosbah keeps only its hash.
apm.autoInjectedNote: Auto-injected on the app's next deploy, so most teams never need to paste this by hand.
apm.rotateHint: The current key stops accepting traces and logs immediately.
apm.snippetHidden: A key already exists; its snippet was shown once when it was created. Rotate to get a new one.
apm.snippetHiddenHint: Rotate to get a new one.
apm.endpointsHint: Request counts and duration percentiles per (method, route), from the root/server spans the SDK exported.
apm.emptyEndpointsHint: Traces appear once the app's OTel SDK is exporting to the endpoint above.
apm.noTraces: No recent traces for this endpoint.
apm.errorsHint: Grouped exceptions from span events and error-level logs, newest occurrence first.
apm.emptyErrorsHint: Exceptions appear once the app's SDK reports one, or logs an ERROR-severity record.
apm.noStacktrace: No stacktrace stored for this exception.

cache.title: Edge cache
cache.hint: Cache this app's responses in a Varnish container in front of it, on its own server — off by default.
cache.enableHint: Applies to the app's server at once.
cache.ttlHint: How long a cached response is served before it is fetched again.
cache.bypassPathsHint: Requests to these paths always skip the cache, e.g. /admin or /api.
cache.bypassCookiesHint: Requests carrying any of these cookies always skip the cache, e.g. session.
cache.statsHint: Read off the Varnish container opportunistically — not a live counter.
cache.purgeHint: Bans every one of the app's hostnames from the cache right now.
cache.disabledHint: Turn the cache on to set a TTL and bypass rules.

monitors.name: Name
monitors.emptyHint: Add an uptime check on one of this site's hostnames, or a rule on its server's CPU, memory or disk.
monitors.deleteBody: Its incident history goes with it.
monitors.incidentsHint: What fired and when it recovered, newest first.
monitors.dialogHint: An incident opens after two failed checks in a row (uptime) or one reading over the limit (resources), and closes on the first pass.
monitors.urlHint: Must be one of this site's own hostnames.
monitors.urlNoHosts: This site has no hostnames yet; add one in the proxy manager first.
monitors.webhookHint: https only. Receives JSON with event, monitor, app, reason, value and at.
monitors.pingUrlHint: Shown once, now — it is not shown again. A GET or POST to it, at least this often, keeps the monitor passing.
monitors.noChannels: No notification channels yet — add one in team settings.

schedules.search: Search by name, command or cron…
schedules.emptyHint: Run a command on a cron expression inside this site's live release, with its environment.
schedules.deleteBody: Its run history goes with it.
schedules.pickRun: Pick a run to read its output.
schedules.outputHidden: Output is for people who can read this site's logs.
schedules.dialogHint: The command runs inside the live release's web container. A run still going when the next time comes is skipped.
schedules.commandHint: A shell line, run as `sh -lc` in the container.

queues.needsDeployer: Queue status and failed jobs can hold the site's data, so they need the deployer role.
queues.none: No queue system was found in this site.
queues.unreadable: A queue system was found, but its state cannot be read from here.
queues.dash: A dash means the number could not be read; it is never a guess.
queues.failedHint: Payloads stay on the server; only the job, its queue and the first line of the error are shown.
queues.search: Search by job, queue or error…
queues.retryAllBody: Every failed job goes back on its queue.
queues.flushBody: Every failed job is deleted. This cannot be undone.
queues.truncated: Only the newest failed jobs are listed.

workers.needsDeployer: Worker status, restart, stop and start need the deployer role: a process's environment and command can be as sensitive as its logs.
workers.notLive: Nothing is live yet. Deploy the site to see its processes here.
workers.stopBody: The container stops but is not removed, so Start reuses it. This does not affect other processes.

storage.volumesHint: Folders that survive deploys, mounted into every release and worker.
storage.noVolumes: No volumes. Files a release writes are lost on the next deploy.
storage.appliesNext: It applies from the next deploy or restart.
storage.pathHint: An absolute path inside the container, such as /app/storage. System folders are refused.
storage.volumeMounted: The live release still mounts this volume. Removing it takes effect on the next deploy; its data can only be deleted once it is no longer mounted.
storage.volumeDataHint: Removing the volume unmounts it. Deleting its data cannot be undone.
storage.bucketsHint: On a MinIO service on this server. Each bucket gets its own key, limited to that bucket, injected as sealed variables.
storage.noMinio: There is no MinIO service on this server yet. Create one first:
storage.bucketDialogHint: The key is limited to this bucket. The variables apply from the next deploy or restart.
storage.bucketRemoveHint: The key is revoked and its variables are removed from the site. The bucket itself is kept unless you delete its data.
storage.force: Delete even if it is not empty
storage.noBrowser: There is no file browser yet: files are read and written by the site itself.

realtime.suggested: This looks like {kind}; the form is filled in from:
realtime.processHint: A worker process from hosbah.toml, without the worker: prefix. It cannot be web.
realtime.portHint: The port the process listens on inside its container.
realtime.pathHint: Requests under this path on the site's hostnames go to the socket server.
realtime.enabledHint: Route websocket traffic to this process
realtime.appliesNext: Saved. It takes effect on the next deploy or restart.
realtime.removeBody: Websocket traffic stops reaching the process at once. The process itself keeps running until the next deploy.
realtime.noteListen: The process must listen on 0.0.0.0 (not 127.0.0.1) inside its container, and PORT is not set for it: give it the port in its command or environment.
realtime.noteDeploy: During a deploy the old socket server keeps serving until the switch; open connections drop when the old release drains, so clients should reconnect.
realtime.noteKeys: Keys, secrets and allowed origins (REVERB_APP_KEY and the like) are the site's own variables. Set them in
realtime.noteConnections: Live connection counts are not shown: none of these servers exposes a dependable local count.

browsers.emptyHint: A headless Chromium on this site's server, for crawling, screenshots, PDFs and tests.
browsers.dialogHint: The first one on a server downloads the browser image, which can take a few minutes.
browsers.removeHint: The browser is stopped and its variables are removed from the site.
browsers.noteConnect: Connect with any CDP client (Puppeteer, Playwright, chromedp) using the WS_ENDPOINT variable; it already carries the token.
browsers.notePrivate: The browser listens only on the server's private address, behind its token. It is never reachable from the internet.
browsers.noteViewer: There is no live view of a session yet.

stacks.installedHint: Each runs in its own limited container on the site's server, linked through sealed variables.
stacks.none: Nothing installed yet. Pick something from the catalog below.
stacks.catalogHint: Ready apps to install next to a site, and starter stacks for a new site. Every recipe pins its image and states its licence.
stacks.installHint: Secrets are generated for it and injected into this site as sealed variables from the next deploy.
stacks.hostnameHint: Optional. Exposes its web UI on this hostname through the proxy manager.
stacks.needsService: This recipe needs a running data service on the same server; create it under the server's Databases first.
stacks.needsMySQL: There is no MySQL/MariaDB service on this server yet. Create one first:
stacks.removeHint: The container is removed along with the hostname and variables it created. Its data is kept unless you delete it.
stacks.publishLater: Publishing your own recipes is coming; the format is built for it, and needs review and signing first.

resources.title: Resources
resources.hint: Memory and CPU caps. Saving here applies live to the running container(s) — no redeploy needed.
resources.baseHint: Applies to every process unless overridden below.
resources.processesHint: Give a process its own limit instead of the base one.
resources.importedHint: This service was imported; Hosbah does not manage its resources.
